clue.text: In court case, copper's facing a charge

indicators.note: the court case is split open and the copper-and-a pair goes in the middle

parts.note: a legal case brought in court is an action
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A police officer faces an accusation of their own in a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal, symbol Cu. 'Facing' just places CU'S beside A.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal charge laid against someone is an allegation of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Assistant runs away from attacker

indicators.note: the runs go away from the attacker, so those letters are taken out of it

parts.note: a raider is someone who attacks
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run, so two runs give two Rs

explanation.surface: A helper flees from an assailant.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Rs are removed from RAIDER, one at each end.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, as to a minister.

clue.text: Group member spoke, substituting Arabic for English

indicators.note: one piece is put in place of another, here Arabic taking English's place
with substituting, says which piece is put in and which taken out

parts.note: to commune is to talk intimately, so spoke is communed

explanation.surface: Someone talked, swapping Arabic for English mid-conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: The last E of COMMUNED becomes AR.
explanation.definitionFit: A communard is a member of a commune, a communal group, or of the Paris Commune of 1871.

clue.text: Old cars used in safari holidays, so to speak

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is pronounced rather than spelt as given

parts.note: a hunting safari is a shooting break, a holiday for shooting game

explanation.surface: Vintage vehicles were driven on hunting trips in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: A shooting brake is an old British estate car, originally built to carry hunting parties; BREAKS and BRAKES sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting brakes are old-fashioned estate cars with a long roof and rear door.

clue.text: For motorist, it could be fifth set of best clothes?

definitions.text: For motorist, it could be fifth
definitions.meaning: the highest gear of a car, often fifth
one's finest outfit, read as clothing at its peak

explanation.definitionFit: The highest gear in a gearbox is the top one, and 'gear' also means clothing.

clue.text: Little jerks in stone? That's some kind of illusion

indicators.note: the little jerks are placed inside the stone

parts.note: an opal is a precious stone
a tic is a small involuntary jerk or twitch

explanation.surface: Tiny twitches seen in a gem turn out to be a trick of the eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerks' is plural but the piece is a single TIC, a loose fit typical of older puzzles. The definition is the adjective that completes 'optical illusion'.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion is a trick of vision, so the word names that kind of illusion.

clue.text: Telephoned newspaper about noon

indicators.note: the newspaper goes around the noon letter

parts.note: a rag is a slang term for a low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone called a paper around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Rang is the past tense of ring, to phone someone.

clue.text: Taking wrong turn, when fog endlessly creeps in

indicators.note: the shortened fog slips inside the word for when

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: the fog loses its final letter

parts.note: mist is a thin fog

explanation.surface: Fog gradually rolls in as someone takes a wrong turning.
explanation.walkthrough: MIST loses its T ('endlessly') to give MIS, which 'creeps in' to AS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss has gone wrong, as when matters take a bad turn.

clue.text: Soldiers involved in risky venture under raw commando

indicators.note: in a down clue the soldiers-in-bet piece sits below the raw piece

parts.note: green means raw or inexperienced

indicators.note: the soldiers are put inside the risky venture

parts.note: a bet is a wager, a risky venture
RE, the Royal Engineers, is a corps of British soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are drawn into a dangerous mission led by an untried commando.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldiers' looks like the definition, but the answer is the single commando.
explanation.definitionFit: A Green Beret is a commando, from the beret worn by British and US special forces.

clue.text: Characters in rhyme — you may find them incredible

definitions.text: Characters in rhyme — you may find them incredible

parts.words: Characters in rhyme — you may find them incredible
parts.note: the creatures of a nursery rhyme, who cannot see; 'incredible' is a pun, the blind being unable to see anything and the tale hard to credit

explanation.definitionFit: The title creatures of the nursery rhyme, three sightless rodents chased by the farmer's wife.

clue.text: Silent, old movie classic

parts.note: dumb means unable to speak, silent

explanation.surface: A silent film from the old days is a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silent, old' suggests a silent-era film, but Dumbo is the 1941 Disney cartoon about a flying elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: Dumbo is a classic Disney animated film.

clue.text: Tree stump finally buried in hole near ravine

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground

indicators.note: the chosen letter is put inside the ravine

parts.note: a chine is a deep narrow ravine, especially on the Isle of Wight and in Dorset

indicators.note: takes only the last letter of stump

explanation.surface: A tree stump ends up buried in a pit beside a gorge.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch pine is a North American pine tree yielding resinous timber.

clue.text: Demand to speak to warders by phone? Use pressure

definitions.text: Demand to speak to warders by phone?
definitions.meaning: jokingly, to connect prison guards ('screws' in slang) to a telephone call
to coerce someone by force or threats

explanation.definitionFit: Screws are old instruments of torture, so applying them means coercing; 'screws' is also prison slang for warders.

clue.text: Smoother version of The Mirror?

parts.note: The Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper, and a mirror is a looking glass, so a 'glass' kind of newspaper; really an abrasive sheet for smoothing wood

explanation.definitionFit: Abrasive sheet coated with powdered glass, used like sandpaper for smoothing surfaces.

clue.text: Trainee left, one due to be paid

parts.note: an earner is someone who earns, who is due wages

explanation.surface: An apprentice leaves; they were owed wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone in training, such as a learner driver.

clue.text: After party, I swallowed mint, perhaps

parts.note: Lab is short for Labour, the British political party
ate means swallowed food

explanation.surface: After a party, someone ate some mint.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an example: mint belongs to the labiate family, plants with lipped flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Mint is a labiate, one of the plant family with two-lipped flowers.

clue.text: Surprise setter appears in top grade puzzle books

indicators.note: the setter is seen inside the run of other pieces

parts.note: A is the top grade in exams
a maze is a puzzle of paths
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: To their surprise, the crossword setter turns up in first-rate puzzle books.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazement is great surprise or wonder.

clue.text: Short article in Herald Tribune featured team's exclusion

definitions.text: Short article in Herald Tribune featured

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a bar is a ban or exclusion

explanation.surface: A brief newspaper piece reports a team's ban.
explanation.walkthrough: A sidebar is the American term for a short article boxed alongside a main story, hence the US paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidebar is a short supplementary item printed alongside a main newspaper story.

clue.text: Slimmer employee altering price tickets during sale

definitions.text: employee altering price tickets during sale
definitions.meaning: a worker who marks prices down

explanation.definitionFit: A reducer is someone who reduces, either body weight or the prices of goods.

clue.text: Trick? This bridge hand might not make one

definitions.meaning: a piece of chicanery, a deceitful ploy

definitions.text: This bridge hand might not make one
definitions.meaning: in bridge, a hand holding no trumps, unlikely to win a trick

explanation.definitionFit: Chicane means trickery, and in bridge it is a hand without trumps.

clue.text: Amerindians, including mostly old natives of Louisiana

indicators.note: the Amerindians hold the shortened word inside them

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people of Canada

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Native Americans included most of the old inhabitants of Louisiana.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' turns OLD into OL, which goes inside CREES.
explanation.definitionFit: Creoles are people of Louisiana descended from early French and Spanish settlers.

clue.text: Articles in haberdashery store causing a sensation

definitions.meaning: small sewing items sold in a shop selling such goods
the prickling feeling in a limb that has gone numb

explanation.definitionFit: Sewing pins and needles are sold by haberdashers, and the phrase also names a tingling sensation.

clue.text: Woman on Ml, foolishly hogging middle of carriageway

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take over the middle piece, holding it inside
signals that the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway, written as M and 1, read as the letter I

indicators.note: takes the central letter of carriageway

explanation.surface: A woman drives badly on the motorway, hogging the centre lane.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is a British motorway; its 1 is read as I. ON and MI are rearranged into NOMI, which holds A.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a woman's name, as of the biblical mother-in-law of Ruth.

clue.text: Titled man given time in prison

indicators.note: the titled man is given the time piece, taken into his name

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight

explanation.surface: A knight is sentenced to time in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is British slang for prison.

clue.text: Language used in complicated cover plan

indicators.note: the letters of cover plan are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A language is used in an elaborate cover story.
explanation.definitionFit: Provencal is the Romance language of Provence in southern France.

clue.text: One composer's no good time for another one

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of another, time instead of good

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: One composer is no good, time for a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No good' removes G from I + BERG and 'time for' puts T in its place.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Ibert was a French composer, so he is another of that profession.

clue.text: Check Friesians regularly

indicators.note: takes every second letter of Friesians

explanation.surface: Inspect the Friesian cattle at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: Friesians are a breed of black and white dairy cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to check or restrain, as with a horse's reins.

clue.text: Gold's what one expected, at first

definitions.text: Gold's what one expected, at first

indicators.note: places the expected piece before the gold piece

parts.note: a prospect is something expected or looked forward to
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: The gold was just what one had hoped for at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes a gold seeker, who hoped to find gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A prospector searches for gold, hoping for a strike.
